channel.title: Conservative Home – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Conservative Home – Bias and Credibility (conservativehome.com)

item.title: Peter Franklin: Farage’s plan to kill the Tories is reaching a dramatic conclusion | Conservative Home
item.description: Kemi Badenoch isn’t just playing defence here. By decisively frustrating Farage’s attempt to kill us off, she might just force Reform to rethink its entire strategy. And once both parties realise they’ve got more important things to worry about than each another, anything is possible.

item.title: Labour should recognise its pensions defeat – and drop mandation | Conservative Home
item.description: The Lords were right to strip ministers of powers that would let them direct investments into pet projects.

item.title: Brandon To: Even a 13-year-old knows crime is out of hand. Why doesn’t the state? | Conservative Home
item.description: In theory, everyone is responsible for crime: the police, the council, community safety partnerships, and central government. In practice, that means no one is accountable. The police point to limited resources. Councils blame the central government. Officials promise to “monitor the situation”.

item.title: Olivier Guitta: We should not underestimate the risks of Iran’s actions in the Strait of Hormuz | Conservative Home
item.description: Iran doesn’t need to win a naval battle. By dumping cheap mines in the Strait, Tehran can freeze not only 20 per cent of the world’s oil but also 5 per cent of global trade. It’s the ultimate asymmetric play: dirt cheap, total gridlock

item.title: Oliver Dean: Releasing LEO data would stop the rise of ‘Mickey-Mouse’ degrees | Conservative Home
item.description: The government spends billions subsidising student loans it knows will never be repaid. The least it can do is give students the information to make better decisions in the first place.

item.title: Our Survey: Big support for Badenoch's position at the start of the Iran war and for increased defence spending | Conservative Home
item.description: 81.2 per cent of responders back Badenoch in saying she'd have granted use of our bases from the start of operations. 62.3 per cent say they backed the US and Israel striking the Iranian regime. 92.8 per cent back the UK spending more on defence, and faster.

item.title: Andrew Gilligan: Britain is in a mess, but not as much as you might think | Conservative Home
item.description: Significant parts of the political debate, on left and right, are based on official statistics which are wrong. And the wrongness more often seems to be in one direction - towards the gloomy, the pessimistic and the negative.

item.title: Fleur Butler: The case for women in power is not fairness – it’s competence | Conservative Home
item.description: Women bring different instincts to group decision-making. They are less inclined towards automatic loyalty and more likely to interrogate assumptions before committing to a course of action.

item.title: Jack Clapper: Is the Conservative Party facing a Liberal-style collapse? | Conservative Home
item.description: As with the Liberals a century ago, there is a growing risk that the Conservative Party’s structure is no longer suited to the electorate it seeks to represent.

item.title: Aarti Joshi: To ‘Back Britain’, we must stop taxing the City out of existence | Conservative Home
item.description: It is time to stop taxing the Stock Exchange out of existence and start powering the next generation of British Tech giants and creating a new generation of shareholders.

item.title: Michael Gray: The Conservative policy on social media for U16's is pro-childhood not anti-tech | Conservative Home
item.description: The impact of social media in schools is visible in friendship groups destabilised overnight by the fallout from group chats; in the heightened anxiety that stems from constant comparison; in the quiet but persistent erosion of self-regulation.

item.title: Katie Lam: We will not fix our problems by telling people to stop talking about them | Conservative Home
item.description: Failure to acknowledge the truth, and a desire to prevent other people from doing so, allowed people to get away with the some of the very worst crimes committed in this country in living memory.

item.title: Our Survey: Majority support North Sea oil and gas exploration amid war in Middle East | Conservative Home
item.description: It should be obvious to the government, as it is to the general public, that the North Sea still has resources to exploit that could help to strengthen Britain's energy security. The thing is that Miliband, and hence Labour’s, net-zero ideology gets in the way.

item.title: Rafe Fletcher: Pro-natalism doesn’t work - communities do | Conservative Home
item.description: Pro-natalists only echo the mistaken belief that the government could and should control fertility rates. His analysis was as wrong as his prescription. Boosting fertility is a bottom-up endeavour. A thriving nation relies upon vigorous communities.

item.title: Charlotte Cadden: It's part of Conservative policing policy that you stay safe on the campaign trail | Conservative Home
item.description: Operation Bridger is the Policing that supports the safety and security of MPs, when MPs are back in their constituencies. It was set up after the horrific murder of Jo Cox MP in 2016 and further enhanced after the murder of Sir David Amess MP in 2021.
